messages:
tom (devex): Quick sync — we need to finalize SDK + docs plan for function-calling + structured outputs before next sprint. Proposal below.

kevin (eng): Agree. Main open questions: exact shaped response for structured outputs (schema envelope) and whether function-calling defaults change.

sara (docs): We need one canonical example for Python + TS each, plus a small migration note for existing users. Keep examples tiny (3-4 lines) and call out types.

maria (pm): Launch criteria suggestion: (1) API contract stable (no breaking changes), (2) TS types compile in strict mode, (3) Python client example uses typed dataclasses, (4) docs page + migration guide live, (5) integration tests pass on Dedicated.

nate (qa): Add acceptance tests: end-to-end call including rerank and embeddings combos. Need prompt set + fuzz for structured parse failures.

kevin (eng): Proposed API change (non-breaking): add optional query param `structured=true` and new response envelope: "{ \"structured\": { \"schema_version\": \"v1\", \"data\": <typed payload>, \"meta\": {...} } }". Function-calling unchanged but SDK helpers should unwrap for convenience.

tom (devex): Draft SDK snippets — short, copyable. Please sanity-check for style and types.

kevin (eng): TS example looks good. Suggest the helper API be `client.callStructured(...)` that returns typed result or throws `StructuredParseError`.

sara (docs): Paste the examples below into the docs playground. Also include a minimal `migration.md` with the one-liner: "If you previously parsed free text, switch to `callStructured` and validate against schema v1."

--- examples ---

tom (devex): TypeScript (stable, strict):
```ts
import Redwood from '@redwood/inference';
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY });

const result = await client.callStructured('gpt-like-model', {
  prompt: 'Return a JSON with {title, steps: string[]}',
  schema: { type: 'object', properties: { title: { type: 'string' }, steps: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } } }, required: ['title', 'steps'] }
});

// result is typed as { title: string; steps: string[] } or throws StructuredParseError
console.log(result.title);
```

tom (devex): Python (py3.11, types):
```py
from redwood import RedwoodClient
from dataclasses import dataclass

client = RedwoodClient(api_key="${RW_KEY}")

@dataclass
class Recipe:
    title: str
    steps: list[str]

out = client.call_structured("gpt-like-model", prompt="Return a JSON with title and steps", schema={"type":"object"})
recipe = Recipe(**out)  # type-checked by mypy
print(recipe.title)
```

--- changelog snippet ---

sara (docs): Add to changelog under Unreleased: `feat(sdk): add callStructured helpers + types for TS and Python; docs + migration guide`

maria (pm): Timeline: aim for runway of 2 weeks: week1 spec + SDK PR, week2 docs + tests + rollout. If customers request rerank integration earlier, we'll prioritize a small example showing embeddings->rerank->structured flow.

kevin (eng): Dev tasks: spec doc (open PR), TS helper impl, Py helper impl, add typed tests, add API flag handling. I can spin up the first PR tomorrow.

nate (qa): I'll create the test matrix and add the prompt fixtures repo entry. @tom can you add the canonical prompts?

tom (devex): Will open a tracking issue with acceptance criteria and link prompts. Quick ask: docs team, can you own the migration note + changelog update? :thumbsup:

sara (docs): Yes — will draft and drop a short review link here by EOD.

ci-bot: Pipeline queued for `sdk/structured-helpers` branch — will run unit tests and typechecks.

kevin (eng): One more: add small note about cost/latency tradeoff when enabling `structured=true` (models may be slightly slower). Add fallback path: if parse fails, return raw text for graceful degradation.

maria (pm): Good call. Add fallback to launch criteria: automatic raw-text fallback + telemetry on parse_failures.

tom (devex): Awesome — I'll collate and create the PR checklist. Thanks everyone.
